implementation_notes: TypeORM maps the association from decorators: @ManyToMany on both entities (with a function returning the inverse) and @JoinTable on the owning side naming the junction table and both foreign-key columns, while the repository inserts and deletes junction rows as the array changes. Junction entities can be promoted to real entities when the association needs payload. This is the decorator-based, Active-Record-adjacent realization and the reason decorators and reflect-metadata must be enabled in tsconfig.
pitfalls: The inverse side must use mappedBy-style function form, and only the owning side writes junction rows - saving from the inverse alone silently does nothing.
Cascade settings decide whether saving an end also saves the other end's rows: cascading on a junction is how unexpected entities get inserted.
Composite keys are not created automatically on the junction table for custom column sets unless the pair is declared unique; duplicate links are otherwise possible.
TypeScript decorators require experimentalDecorators and emitDecoratorMetadata, and strict property initialisation fights entity classes without definite-assignment assertions.

variants.name: Prisma explicit relation model over the join table
variants.implementation_notes: Prisma declares the schema rather than the objects: an implicit m-n needs only the two list fields and Prisma manages the relation table itself, named _CategoryToPost with columns A and B and a unique index over them - the pattern exactly as the database sees it. The explicit form declares the relation table as a model with the two relations, a composite id (@@id([postId, categoryId])) and any payload, and the generated client then requires the link to be created explicitly. Use implicit while the association is a pure pair list and explicit as soon as it carries metadata or must be queried.
pitfalls: Implicit m-n requires both models to have a single @id (no composite ids or @unique) and forbids fields/references/onDelete on the relation; it cannot carry payload.

The implicit relation table's name and A/B columns are a convention (underscore + alphabetical model names + To) - renaming models renames the table, which breaks hand-written SQL that assumed the old name.
Referential actions on the explicit relation model decide orphan behaviour, and the default (Restrict) will refuse to delete an end while links exist.
